business.title: Construction-induced soil compaction in agri-photovoltaic systems: evidence from an Arenosol
business.desc: Agri-photovoltaic (Agri-PV) systems, which combine crop production with solar energy generation, are rapidly expanding across Europe, yet their implications for soil quality remain poorly understood. This study assessed soil compaction following the installation of an Agri-PV system in autumn 2024 on an Arenosol in Brandenburg, Germany. Bulk density (BD) and penetration resistance (PR) were measured across multiple depths after construction finalization. Both parameters were compared to a nearby reference and established agronomic thresholds. Subsoil BD in construction zones (1.67–1.69 g cm⁻³) exceeded root growth thresholds, while PR at mid-depth reached 3.7–4.1 MPa, surpassing the limit for root elongation. Our results align with literature indicating that Arenosols, due to their weak structure and lack of shrink-swell capacity, are highly vulnerable to persistent compaction. The observed compaction poses risks to rooting depth, water infiltration, and crop yield, underscoring the need for targeted mitigation measures. We suggest that pedological construction supervision should become standard practice for Agri-PV projects, ensuring soil protection measures are integrated into planning, construction, and restoration. More flexible policy frameworks and monitoring of soil recovery post-installation are needed for aligning renewable energy expansion with sustainable crop production.

technology.title: Safety and efficacy of rectal spacers in locally advanced prostate cancer
technology.desc: Biodegradable perirectal spacers reduce rectal irradiation and rectal toxicity during radiotherapy for prostate cancer (PCa). However, while their use is well-established in localised PCa, there is minimal data on locally advanced PCa. Objective: to determine safety and efficacy of rectal spacers in patients with cT3 disease. A prospective single-centre cohort study was conducted from 2022 to 2024. Inclusion: consecutive men with mpMRI-directed biopsy-proven cT1 to cT3 PCa, planned for external beam radiotherapy. All patients underwent spacer insertion with either SpaceOAR or Barrigel. Dosimetry ranged from 55 to 79.2 Gy over 20–41 fractions. 181 men were included. 119 (65.7%) had cT1c/cT2 disease, and 62 (34.3%) cT3a/b disease. Post-spacer rectal spacing did not differ significantly between the cT3 and cT1c/cT2 groups at midgland (1 cm ± 0.36 vs. 1.05 cm ± 0.37, p = 0.34) or apex (0.52 cm ± 0.27 vs. 0.59 ± 0.3, p = 0.12); a statistically significant difference was observed at the base (0.94 cm ± 0.32 vs. 0.82 ± 0.3, p = 0.01). Acute grade 1/2 GI toxicity occurred in 12.9% vs. 5.0% of patients (p = 0.06), and late toxicity in 4.3% vs. 1.1% (p = 0.22); neither difference reached statistical significance, and no grade ≥ 3 toxicity was reported in either group. Temporary urinary retention rates did not differ significantly between groups (17.7% vs. 13.4%, p = 0.44), and there was no refractory urinary retention, infective complications, or rectal mucosal injury in either group. Freedom from biochemical failure was 98.1% (51/52) in the cT3 group versus 100% (109/109) in the cT1c/cT2 group over a median follow-up of 8 months. In conclusion, these preliminary findings support the utility, technical feasibility and acceptable short-term safety of rectal spacer insertion in cT3 PCa.

world.title: Reforms Transformed Media, Says Ethiopian Media Authority Director-General
world.desc:
Addis Ababa, August 16, 2026 (ENA) —Ethiopian Media Authority Director-General Haimanot Zeleke said recent reforms have transformed the media by removing licensing bottlenecks, expanding access and content diversity, coupling greater freedom with stronger professional responsibility and capacity-building.
Ethiopia’s media landscape has been significantly reshaped by the reforms, she added.
In an interview with the ENA, the Director-General noted that the changes have enabled media institutions to expand in type, number, accessibility and content, creating a more open and competitive environment for information flow between the public and the government.
“By reforming previous licensing bottlenecks in the media sector, opportunities have been created for numerous professionals and institutions wishing to enter the field,” Haimanot said, adding that this has directly increased participation and diversified content.
According to her, revising preconditions that once constrained the profession has allowed media workers to operate more freely, while stressing that “media freedom must go hand-in-hand with professional responsibility and respect for the law.”
The Authority has also paired this liberalization with efforts to raise standards. She highlighted that training delivered through the Ethiopian Media Excellence Center have graduated selected journalists from various outlets to cultivate reporters who work effectively, inform the public, and bring agendas closer to the people.
The Director-General said capacity-building and content monitoring are being used not only to grow the sector in quantity and reach but also to enhance professional competence and the quality of information provided to citizens.
Addressing digital-era challenges, Haimanot stated that the Authority is working with relevant bodies to curb the spread of false information and hate speech.
Looking ahead, she pledged actions to further strengthen the media landscape and support democratic system-building.
“Support will be provided to ensure healthy media institutions grow further and operate in line with professional ethics and legal principles,” she said, adding that the Authority will educate, train and bring into the legal framework those outlets and professionals not operating along proper professional lines.
The Director-General concluded that ongoing capacity-building aims to ensure media outlets serve as reliable bridges between the public and government, enabling citizens to access accurate information, report issues freely and professionally, and play a constructive role on national matters.
